 Judgment

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 10.06.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 10.06.2022 at about 9.00pm when he was riding his scooter bearing Reg.NO.KA51HN8799 at Gandhibazar Main SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 3294/2022 Road, reached near Karanji Circle at Basavanagudi, a Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA05LD 2577 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, came from right side and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was taken to Victoria Hospital and has undertaken treatment.

So far he has spent Rs.60,000/ towards medical expenses,
conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,

At the time of accident he was a Fish Vendor (Road Side)
and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
Due to accidental injuries he lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock.
The accident caused due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA05LD2577.
The Basavanagudi Police have registered a case against the rider of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.0066/2022.

Therefore, the 1st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2 nd respondent SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 3294/2022 being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons the respondent No.1 did not appear hence placed exparte.
5. The objection of the respondent No.2.
It has stated that there is a delay of 6 days in filing the complaint.
It has contended that petitioner has suffered only clavicle injuries there were no damages to his eye.
The petition is bad for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
It is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
It denies having insured the Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA05 LD2577.
The rider did not have valid and effective DL and the vehicle did not have a valid FC as on the date of accident.
The petitioner was riding the scooter without wearing the helmet.
It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of SCCH - 25 5 MVC No. 3294/2022 accident.

It Mohammed Saeed Sulthan Alias Sayeed vs Meghana B. Yadav on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188376491/
2 contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 10.06.2022 at about 9.00pm due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA51HN 8799 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What order or award?
7.
The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.13.
He has also got examined Mr.Hagaraja G.V.  Medical Record Technician and got marked Exs.P.14 to 16.
Dr.S.Ramachandra got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.17 & P.18.
Ms. Asma Khanam Bi - eye witness got examined as PW.4 and got SCCH - 25 6 MVC No. 3294/2022 marked Ex.P.19.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following decisions:
1. 2011 ACJ 1434 (SC) (DB) : Nagarajappa Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Ins. Co.
Ltd.,
2. 2015 ACJ 721 (SC) (DB) : Jakir Hussein Vs. Sabir and Ors.
3. 2014 ACJ 2550 (SC) (DB) : Kiran Vs sajjan Singh and Ors.

Issue No.1: In to prove that the accident occurred due to the SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 3294/2022 actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA05LD 2577, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.7.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination he has stated that, he was waiting in the signal when the accident occurred.
He has admitted that the FIR was filed after 6 days of the accident.
There was no surgery of eye in Victoria hospital.
He has also got examined the MRO of Victoria hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.14 to P.16 Authorization letter, MLC register extract and case file.
During his cross examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.

sentences.text: During her cross examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The Respondent No.2 insurer has denied that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Suzuki Access and contended that the petitioner did not wear helmet.
In order to prove their contention they have not led any evidence.
The FIR was registered after 6 days of the accident and it is admitted by the doctor that the petitioner has taken treatment for 6 days.
Therefore, it is clear that the delay is properly explained.
The IMV report at Ex.P.5 shows that both the vehicles have suffered damages.
The wound certificate at Ex.P.6 shows that the petitioner has suffered the clavicle injuries and other injuries in an RTA on 10.06.2022.
The police have filed the charge sheet against the offending bike after thorough investigation and the accused was also found drunk at the time of accident.
Therefore, on the basis of police records and medical records, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA05LD2577.

Accordingly,
issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6.

As per Ex.P.6, the Petitioner has SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 3294/2022 sustained (i) Fresh cut lacerated wound right eyebrow, (ii) Abrasion over left Index finger base and (iii) Swelling and restricted mobility left shoulder and as per Xray it shows fracture of lateral 1/3rd of left clavicle.
Doctor opined out of these injuries, injury Nos.1 & 2 are simple and injury No.3 is grievous in nature.
13. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.S.Ramachandra as PW.3.
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed midshaft clavicle fracture left.

He further stated that the petitioner is suffering from disability of left shoulder girdle and left upper limb at 16.25%
and to the whole body at 5.42%.
14.
PW.3 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has admitted that petitioner took treatment in Victoria hospital as an inpatient for 6 days.
Petitioner can carryout his work with some difficulties.
The fractures are united and implants are in situ.

sentences.text: On perusal of the evidence of PW.3 and the fractures suffered by the petitioner since he is a Fish seller and he suffered only clavicle injury, this court deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 5.42%.

Monthly income:
16.

The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was a Fish Seller and earning Rs.25,000/
per month.
In this SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 3294/2022 regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,500/ per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 24 years as could be made out from Ex.P.11/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.
The accident took place in the year 2022.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Victoria Hospital,
Bangalore wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 11.06.2022 to 16.06.2022 and was diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.9.

Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/
under this head.
SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 3294/2022  ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.60,000/ towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.12 for a sum of Rs.1,595/
There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Victoria Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.

Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,500/
under this head.

5 SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 3294/2022 iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P.11, the date of birth of the petitioner is 24.08.1998 and the date of accident is 10.06.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 24 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,81,462/
(Rs.15,500/ x 12 x 18 x 5.42%= Rs.1,81,462/) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained simple and grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 5.42% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner SCCH - 25 14 MVC No.
3294/2022 has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of the PW.3, the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants from left clavicle.
In this regard the petitioner or the Pw.3 have not produced any estimation letter.
Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injuries, evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.
SCCH - 25 15 MVC No. 3294/2022 (viii) LOSS OF MARRIAGE PROSPECTS:
The petitioner has averred that he has lost better chances of marriage due to the disability suffered by him.
The court has assessed the functional disability at 5.42%.
Therefore, looking at the nature of injuries, evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.10,000/ is awarded under this head.

17. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.50,000/
2.
Medical expenses Rs. 1,595/
